notes.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Day 7: Churnotsavam and Indra Vimanam
notes.occasion: Brahmotsavam Day 7: Churnotsavam and Indra Vimanam
body: 10:00 AM: Thirumanjanam
✅04:30 PM: Churnotsavam (Procession)
✅08:30 PM: Procession on Indra Vimanam – Thathacharya said: what is different about him tonight? He has no shankha chakra. He is Indra! Narayanaad indro jayate" (नारायणाद् इन्द्रो जायते)

Brahmotsavam Day 7. We’re a bit late coming to the Churnotsavam, and have missed the turmeric pounding part. This is a ceremony that brings Perumal and Thayar together, so it happens notably after the Thirukalyanam. Turmeric powder (the auspicious among auspicious powders) is prepared and ceremonially offered or exchanged (to celebrate an auspicious union among auspicious unions!). No playful throwing or sprinkling of the turmeric powder happens here, though that may have been a little holi like. Next, there appears to be a Nel Alavu sevai. We think this is a Mudaliar community ubhayam event as we see Raja sir there (who often comes to our aid in making sure we have access and permission to photograph in several temples we see him in, not to mention making sure we get our share of prasadam).

notes.title: Ghousiga Balasubramaniya Koyil Vaikasi Vishakam Day 2, Shanmukha Purappadu
body: We went to this but caught the procession on their way. The route is down the road next to Ghousiga, then Nehru St., then back on MG road. A bit of a lonely procession. Through market areas with no houses or people coming out with archanai thattu. Pulled by a temple-owned tractor! With some fairly uninterested looking guys.

notes.title: Sundara Vinayaka, Vaikasi Vishakam
body: The Ghousiga procession goes past Sundara Vinayaka, and we get pulled into the koyil, run by Rani Ma’m’s family whom we met at the Vastu puja at the Sivan koyil. Cutest place with a little ther of its own to do ul-purappadu. Sapta Matrikas, Hanuman – Natarajar and mini-Naalvar all. She’s the 4th generation in charge of the place. Ladies and their children mostly running the place. Felt like we were called there. Very simple, homey, low-key puja.

notes.title: Nandikeswara Koyil, Vaikasi Vishakam
body: Dewan Kandappa sent us a notice for Vishakam observances at Nandikeswara:
4:30pm onwards: Special Tirumañjanam for Sri Jñāna Velayudha Swami, accompanied by Sri Valli and Devasena
6:00 p.m. onwards: Peroḷi (the great light) worship in a special decoration, followed by the recitation of Thiruppugazh.
7:00 p.m. onwards: a spiritual discourse on “The Marriage of Sri Valli and Murugan,” delivered by Mrs. Dr. V. Sankaradevi. The Dewan kindly shared the temple’s recordings of this session here.
Vaisaki Vishakam starts 10:38am onwards, until May 30,1:20 pm

notes.title: Lawspet Murugan Koyil Vaikasi Vishakam, Satru Samhara Trishati Homam and Laksharchana
notes.occasion: Vaikasi Vishakam, Satru Samhara Trishati Homam and Laksharchana
body: We could not attend the Rathotsavam on the night before, there was just no way, so it’s on our list for the next year. This morning begins pretty much on time at 530am with a kalasa puja to three kalasas, presumably Murugan, Valli and Devasena. All 6 priests present stand by the kalasas which are arranged on a stand behind the agni kundam, and it’s quite a sight when all six do deeparadhanai, though only one priest holds the classic aradhanai lamp which is brought around to devotees, all else just have the thattu vilakku (plate lamp).

The homam begins next and is performed simultaneously by the six priests, including Narayanaswamy from Mutthumariamman who has been called in to help (He is as amused to see us as we are to see him; tells people at other times: “Avaa Lawspet verraikkum chenthutangaa! They’ve gone as far as Lawspet!) and he asks for photos of course.

This is then followed by the Laksharchanai for which the young priest takes lead, supported by six others. We are aware of a moolavar abhishekam that will have happened, but we miss it since we have to rush back to town to see the Sivan Koyil ther.
We return in the evening around 5 just to see the Murugan moolavar alankaram and to ask about the day.

notes.title: Vedapuriswara Koyil Brahmotsavam Day 9 Rathotsavam, Vaikasi Vishakam
body: ✅7:00 AM - 8:30 AM - Rathotsavam (Temple Chariot Festival)
6:00 PM - Abhishekam.

Brahmotsavam Day 9, the day of the chariot! We arrive as the homam concludes. Even before the deities board the ther, there is magic in the aradhanai that preceded it under the rays of the rising sun. The utsava murtis are kept outside the library-mandapam. We see the completion of the homam; and piercing this sacrificial smoke are the rays of the morning  sun meeting the flames of the aradhanai. The deities proceed to an ul-purappadu after which Somaskandar is raised and seated onto the ther. The ropes are grasped, the wheel-blocks are removed, and after the last of the aradhanais – pull! The ratha of Somaskanda rolls ahead. The ther’s journey around the madaveethi lasts long, and is significantly obstructed by cables and trees, which necessitate immediate chopping and slashing.

Later in the day we do a recording with Thirunavukkarasar Odhuvar. He spoke about the Malaimatri padigam, malai-matri or the malai of words that stays the same when turned around or recited forwards and backwards–effectively a palindrome:
யாமாமாநீ யாமாமா யாழீகாமா காணாகா
காணாகாமா காழீயா மாமாயாநீ மாமாயா
This first line read backwards makes the second line. Discourses can be given on these lines and their poetic construction, but here is a rough translation:
“Are we gods? No. You alone are truly God—yes, indeed!
O great Lord who plays the yaazh, O One of irresistible beauty!
O One who wears serpents openly, O One who made Kama invisible!
O Lord of Kazhi [Sirkazhi], O great Maya! Remove us from the dark impurities of maya.”
This is the third Thirumurai Tevaram song composed by Thirugnanasambandhar. It belongs to the 'Thirumalaimarthu' genre of pictorial poetry for the Sirkazhi Tirutthalam

notes.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Day 8
body: Vennai Thazhi and Horse Vahana in the evening; Nammalvar Jayanti Abhishekam.

✅07:00 AM: Vennai Thazhi (Butter Pot) Appearance Procession – with the cutest chaatrified baby backside – Munnilum Pinnazhagiya Perumal (முன்னிலும் பின்னழகிய பெருமாள்), as they say of Namperumal, the processional deity of the Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple.
10:30 AM: Thirumanjanam
08:00 PM: Procession on Horse Vahanam–Thirumangai Alvar sits on the horse named Adalma who carried him across various regions as he traveled to visit and sing praises of the 108 Divya Desams.
It is Nammalvar Jayanti, abhishekam only since it comes in the middle of the Brahmotsavam.
Brahmotsavam Day 8.

notes.title: Kamakshi Amman Koyil Vaikasi Vishakam
body: 8-9am: Murugan Abhishekam

The Murugan abhiskekam is a simple but beautiful affair. Not too many in attendance, but it’s done jointly by Gurukkal (for Murugan) and Periyavar (for the Mayil and vel). A family of the ubhayakarars is sitting on the jamakalam outside and watching us. We tell them about the green tint on the Murugan evident only during paal abhishekam – it’s something they did not know. Enchantments are everywhere. We come back later for a small prasadam.

notes.title: Ghousiga Balasubramaniya Koyil Vaikasi Vishakam Day 3, Murugan Nakshatram Purappadu
notes.occasion: Vaikasi Vishakam Day 3, Murugan Nakshatram Purappadu
body: This is Murugan’s birth day or nakshatra naal, the day of the great processional Mail-aattam! I’m not sure how we come by earlier and do not register that the whole set up to carry and dance with the utsavar on a peacock vahana is being fashioned out of bamboo. Ingenious. There’s a big dance with a matching music (how to describe it in words? It anticipates the sashaying of the peacock tail) at the purappadu point which we do not see. Kadir tells us about it later. But we follow the procession mid-way until it returns to the temple and all deities move indoors. And it’s quite something. The peacock sashays, the kudais dance. The music matches. On return, the Kailaya vadyam is something else – maybe even too intense for the small spaces this temple occupies. No respite, crowds inside, almost nowhere to move, and music loud enough to burst eardrums but so addictive. The moolasthanam is closed for the night; the utsavar here seems to have a life of His own! I guess it’s his birthday, so he deserves a romp around town in full form.

notes.title: VEDAPURISWARA & VARADARAJA PERUMAL: A day of Brahmanda Brahmotsavam Events
notes.occasion: A day of Brahmanda Brahmotsavam Events
body: VEDAPURISWARA SCHEDULE
7:00 AM - Sri Natarajar Theradi Mithitthal Theerthavari.
9:00 AM - Chandrasekarar Theerthavari & Abhishekam.
4:00 PM - Dvaja Avarohanam (Flag Lowering).
7:00 PM - Adhikara Nandi Procession.
PERUMAL
06:00 AM: Commencement of Chariot Festival
06:30 AM - 08:00 AM: Ratharohanam (Chariot Procession) in Mithuna Lagna, followed by Thirumanjanam and Theerthavari
08:00 PM: Dhvajavarohanam (Flag Lowering), Kumbha Prokshanam, Saattrumurai

Vedapuriswara Brahmotsavam Day 10 and Varadaraja Perumal Brahmotsavam Day 9. — The ther at the Perumal Koyil is considerably larger than the Sivan Koyil’s. The wheels are of stone and metal, not wood; Vishwaksena draws the chariot, not Brahma. Perumal is hauled up a flight of stairs and placed in the heart of the chariot. A few moments of preparation, a final aradhanai, and the ther sets off rolling. Perumal is grand and magnificent, but the streets struggle to accommodate him. Tree cover amply obstructs Perumal’s giant chariot. Internet cables running across the road wrap around the ther’s kalasa and kodi. The procession is slow and arduous, inching forward in the gaps of laborious clearance. One great tree on Thiyagaraja Street had to be almost entirely felled so Perumal may pass. We almost miss the Nataraja Theerthavari at the Sivan Koyil because of this, but manage to catch its tail end.

The returning half seemed to pass quicker, and it was soon time for the theerthavari in the late afternoon. Perumal’s and his two consorts’ utsava murtis were set on steps that go down to the kulam. In front of them was also the “astra murti” equivalent – who is perhaps Vishwaksena? Perhaps Perumal himself? [TBC]. Upon completing the thirumanjanam, this astra murti was taken down the steps and, with the priest standing ankle deep in water, was given the Sahasradhara Abhishekam. The conch and chakra shaped vessels poured manjal-neer onto the Sahasradhara plate, showering the murti. In the blazing afternoon sun the sight and sound of the cool, refreshing thousand-fold trickles of water were most temptingly soothing to the senses.

The theerthavari is the last of the events that marks the ending of the Brahmotsavam proper. Later today the flag is lowered from the dhvajastambha, declaring the start of the six-day Vidaiyatri – concluding events.

The Sivan Koyil’s kodi comes down sooner than that of the Perumal Koyil. You can get a sense of what the event sounded like, from the songs of the Odhuvars from that their last day of this Brahmotsavam.

notes.title: Ghousiga Balasubramaniya Koyil Vaikasi Vishakam Day 4: Pancha Murti Purappadu
notes.occasion: Vaikasi Vishakam Day 4: Pancha Murti Purappadu
body: This is a continuation of the utsavam that started with Vishakam. The pancha murtis are VInayaka leading the way, but with Chandikeswara, followed by Murugan with his consorts looking grander than grand, though the consorts are almost hidden by Murugan’s grand swirling garlands, Somaskanda, and finally the Thani Ambal. The pusari we often see in the temple accompanies. Some kids ride along. It is no doubt a grand but somewhat distracted procession. It passes through commercial areas and markets where it seems to meet with reverence and indifference in equal measure.

notes.title: Vedapuriswara Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 1: Theppotsavam
body: ✅10:00 AM - Abhishekam – led by Arasoo swami.
✅7:00 PM - Theppotsavam (Float Festival).
Brahmotsavam Day 11, Vidaiyatri Day 1

Kalasamharamurti alankaram for Theppotsavam. For the Vedapuriswara Koyil the iconography on the theppal is always a samharam or tandavam. Arasoo Swami makes sure we get a ride on the theppal, too! We feel like kids who have been given extra lollipops. We meet the man who has cleaned the kulam. The junior priest acknowledges this and asks him to come for a ride, too, though he demurs.
Another priest speaks to us about two kinds of bhakti – morattuthanamaana bhakti and “silent” bhakti. He observes that the former is growing more prevalent these days.

notes.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 1: 108 Kalasa Thirumanjanam and Dwadasa Aradhanam
notes.occasion: Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 1: 108 Kalasa Thirumanjanam and Dwadasa Aradhanam
body: 10:00 AM: 108 Kalasa Thirumanjanam
04:30 PM: Dwadasa Aradhanam
✅07:00 PM: Chandra Prabhai Procession and Sapthavarna Puranam recitation
Brahmotsavam Day 10, Vidaiyatri Day 1.
The kalasa thirumanjanam happened in the morning for the moolavar. Later there was a dwadasa aradhanam, with the showing of twelve lamps.

The Sapthavarna Puranam recitation was by Ramanan Bhattacharya after the return of the procession. The Sapthavarna Puranam/Sathavaranam Puranam is a traditional devotional text dedicated to Lord Surya, focusing on his 21 names and attributes that remove sins, overcome illness, and bring prosperity.

Saptavaranam, Saptāvaraṇam: Seven square enclosures, one within the other, the innermost containing the central shrine, as at Śrīraṅgam; கோயிலைச் சுற்றி அமைந்த ஏழு பிராகாரங்கள்/ koyilais surri amaintha ezhu piragarangal.

notes.title: Vedapuriswara Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 2
body: 9:00 AM - Naalvar Abhishekam, Thirugnanasambandar Festival
✅7:00 PM - Indira Vimanam Procession.
Brahmotsavam Day 12, Vidaiyatri Day 2
Today is Vaikasi Moola Nakshatram, which marks Thirugnanasambandar’s mukti-day.

Thirugnanasambandar’s utsava murti, characterised by the index finger pointing towards Siva and Parvati in the heavens above, is brought to the Naalvar shrine. They are given a fairly long abhishekam, following which Thirugnanasambandar moves out and straight across to Natarajar Mandapam, where he will be dressed and adorned. With him also moves the modest crowd present. Once ready, he is presented an aradhanai, taken on a purappadu around the prakaram, and then taken straight into the sanctum of his Lord. There’s a woman I see often who is telling me about this – he will receive now the jnana paal, or the milk of wisdom from the Divine Mother. He first faces his Lord, and then diagonally faces the Ambal murti there who gives him the milk of Siva’s wisdom – Siva Jnanam. Lights go off completely for this. The Garba griha is filled with lamplight. It’s one of those unforgettable moments, which is unforgettable because it’s there and gone in a blink.

notes.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 2: Theppotsavam
body: 10:30 AM: Thirumanjanam
✅07:00 PM: Theppotsavam (Float Festival)

Brahmotsavam Day 11, Vidaiyatri Day 2. Perumal is in Kaliyadamana alankaram for Theppotsavam. Here too, as in the Sivan Koyil, the Theppal alankaram is always in an ugra form. The theppal’s circular structure creates a halo, inside which Krishna dances taming the serpent. His right foot planted firmly on the centre of the hood, left foot aloft in dance, left hand grasping Kaliya’s tail and right hand holding the flute – the form is indeed befitting for a scene in the waters.

notes.title: VEDAPURISWARA & VARADARAJA PERUMAL Vidaiyatri’s long, slow endings
body: VEDAPURISWARA SCHEDULE
10:00 AM - Abhishekam.
✅7:00 PM - Unjal Utsavam (Swing Festival)
VARADARAJA PERUMAL SCHEDULE
10:00 AM: Thirumanjanam
07:00 PM: MutthuVimanam Purappadu

Brahmotsavam Day 13 and Brahmotsavam Day 12 respectively, for Sivan and Perumal; Vidaiyatri Day 3 for both. Already we have a sense of the festivals coming to a close with these reposed finales. Umamaheswara sits on a swing in the warm night air, a Mutthu Vimanam simpler by far than the one we saw for the Ramar Utsavam some months before carrying Perumal out with his consorts. These are scenes of beauty, the pastimes of the Gods, their slow withdrawal from the peak intensities of the festivals carried out in their own names.

notes.title: VEDAPURISWARA & VARADARAJA PERUMAL Vidaiyatri’s long, slow endings
body: VEDAPURISWARA SCHEDULE
9:00 AM - Abhishekam.
✅7:00 PM - Sri Chandikeswarar Utsavam
VARADARAJA PERUMAL SCHEDULE
10:00 AM: Thirumanjanam
✅07:00 PM: Pushpa Prabhai (Floral Procession)

Brahmotsavam Day 14 and Brahmotsavam Day 13 respectively, for Sivan and Perumal; Vidaiyatri Day 4 for both. You know things are really closing up when there’s a whole utsavam to Chandikeswara– he’s the last to be offered food before closing the temple at night, the one who follows the processional parades, the great devotee who sits nearby, but outside. And the Perumal Koyil holds grand court as Rajagopalan with a sengkol in his hand, peacock feathers in his hair, and cows at his feet, Sri Devi and Bhu Devi turn into Rukmini and Satyabama. One has a sense of peace, justice and plenty descending on the world.

It’s perhaps fitting that Rajagopal Thathacharya give us some apt closing lines – as he often does, he calls us aside with twinkling eyes and a deeply happy smile because such is the way he takes delight in stories of the Lord, and recites (of course at a moment when the nadaswaram makes it hard to hear anything, even if we are listening with rapt attention) Paasuram 1.1.9 of the Thiruvaymozhi:
உளன் எனில் உளன் அவன் உருவம் இவ் உருவுகள்
உளன் அலன் எனில், அவன் அருவம் இவ் அருவுகள்
உளன் என இலன் என இவை குணம் உடைமையில்
உளன் இரு தகைமையொடு ஒழிவு இலன் பரந்தே.
uḷaṉ eṉil uḷaṉ avaṉ uruvam iv uruvukaḷ
uḷaṉ alaṉ eṉil, avaṉ aruvam iv aruvukaḷ
uḷaṉ eṉa ilaṉ eṉa ivai kuṇam uṭaimaiyil
uḷaṉ iru takaimaiyoṭu oḻivu ilaṉ parantē.
If it is said "He exists," He exists, and all these forms are His forms.
If it is said "He exists not," He is formless, and all these formless things are His formlessness.
Because He possesses both these attributes—of existing and non-existing,
He exists in both natures, spread everywhere without end.
There’s still another Vidaiyatri day ahead, but could there be better lines to end a festival of this sort really?

notes.title: Vedapuriswara Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 5 Vidaiyatri Abhishekam and Thirumurai Utsavam
notes.occasion: Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 5 Vidaiyatri Abhishekam and Thirumurai Utsavam
body: 9:00 AM - Vidaiyatri Abhishekam.
7:00 PM - Thirumurai Utsavam
Brahmotsavam Day 15, Vidaiyatri Day 5

More special than we imagined. Ayyappan swami had said in the morning when I went with Dyuman that today Gurumama would be the Instagram star (ha ha ha). Indeed, it was special. 12 Thirumurai all dressed up to look much like a siva lingam. Naalvar abhishekam in the morning, and they’re propitiated and taken out in procession (ethir sevai), followed by the thirumurai, and finally Chandrasekara and Gauri. Pushpaka vimana alankaram for Siva on Vrushabha. The Naalvar got a chariot, as did the Thirumurai.

Each year a group is called in to sing Thirumurai songs – a mixed bunch this time, not at all all from the Thirumurai. Yennappan allava, from the Nandanar Charitram by Gopalakrishna Bharati. Naada Bindu, which is Thiruppugazh’s last song. Nadaswaram played முத்தைத்தரு பத்தித் திருநகை – which again is Thiruppugazh. “Thodudaiya Seviyan” is a favorite, but I’ve only heard it sung once at the Chandikeswara abhishekam deeparadhanai. The group this time were young girls from Chennai led by a teacher. Each year there’s a different group to sing. I guess it’s a way of encouraging the classical arts and singing in general, which is for its own sake lovely.

notes.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 5 Unjal Utsavam
body: 10:00 AM: Thirumanjanam
07:00 PM: Unjal Utsavam (Swing Festival)

Brahmotsavam Day 14, Vidaiyatri Day 5. We arrived super late to this, thanks to the delays in the Thirumurai utsavam, expecting to see Perumal in the Vasanta Mandapam swing as it’s been before. But no. He had other plans! When we reached the ardhajama puja was basically concluding. Nadaswarams playing Annamayya’s “Brahmam okate!” Perumal was nicely ensconced in an embellished  kannadi-AC room with lovely Thanjavur paintings on either side, deep within the chamber next to the Kodandarama shrine – fancy! Sitting to the left of his 2 consorts, typical raja style, instead of between them, as usual. We saw the last aradhanai just before closing.
Perumal’s utsavar already back in the moola sthanam from earlier in the day, Ramanan Bhattacharya said.

notes.title: Vedapuriswara Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 6 Utsava Shanti and Shankhabhishekam
notes.occasion: Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 6 Utsava Shanti and Shankhabhishekam
body: 9:00 AM - Utsava Shanti, Shankhabhishekam (Conch Abhishekam).
Brahmotsavam Day 16, Shankhabhishekam

Went for this at 10:30am. Homam going on, Arjun gurukkal (who was the main priest during the whole Brahmotsavam) leading. Abhishekam was happening, we caught the tail end of it. Homa finished, the 2 kalasa were taken by Arjun and Kalyana Sundara Gurukkals one round about the prakaram, coconut phat near the dhvajastambha, and then the main kalasa into the moola sthanam – Presumably 108 shankha for abhishekam, done one by one unlike Chetty Koyil where it was being done a few at a time – then shift over to Amman sannathi for the second kalasa pour – simple alankaram and deeparadhanai.

notes.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri Day 6: Panaka Puja
body: 5:00 PM: Panaka Puja
Brahmotsavam Day 15. Ramanan Bhattacharya said there will be a Vizhithikaappu, washing with veneer or hot water— afternoon puja not for public viewing, followed by Panaka Puja.

notes.title: Angalamman Koyil Muthialpet Theipirai Ashtami, Kali Abhishekam
body: We’d not seen this one together so went together. Quiet temple evening. Climbed up onto the terrace to see the Parashakti figure being attended to by some lads who were grouped there–the temple gives them this work and these socialities. Below, the two main priests prepare for and conduct the entire abhishekam. No additional helpers. They’re swift and efficient. Alankaram does not take hours. Invariably there’s a kunkumarchanai with namavali chanting (is this the same as a Navavarna puja?). The temple always has a distinctly open community feel, it’s like a place where people gather to learn and be together. They accept the tutelage of the Iyers, who are avuncular figures to them. It’s just a very nice, almost intimate atmosphere here always. Sriram Gurukkal sends us photos and videos from time to time, and we share with him. too. The casual, easy nature of these things extends that feel of place.

notes.title: Conversation with Dr. K. Vadivelou on temple cultures of music and dance
notes.occasion: Conversation with Dr. K. Vadivelou on temple cultures of music and dance
body: I (Deepa) meet Vadivelou Sir at his footwear shop close to the Nandikeswara temple. Conversation ranges widely from his own research on dance and literary forms, the devadasi tradition (and what the loss of the tradition has meant for temple cultures generally), to panchamukha vadyam and the rules of its use as a ritual instrument (each face for separate jatis), to various facts and details about the Nandikeswara temple, and to music in general. This note is not a summary, but an acknowledgement that things he said he woke me to

(1) the importance of music and dance in temple cultures as creating not merely atmosphere but auspiciousness (therefore, indeed, the term “mangala vadyam” or the instrument which generates mangalam)--and the integration of nadaswaram traditions with dance, which also aspects destroyed by the abolishment of the devadasi tradition;

(2) likewise the roles of othuvars and araiyars (offering araiyar cevai) using mudras in their enactments of hymns and songs – they are not merely recitations, but enactments – so should we think of tantric puja forms similarly then, as enactments?;

(3) I had a picture of the temple as coming alive in the evenings, with devadasi groups resident nearby, dedicated to specific temples, dancing and “gesturing” during sayarakshai and palliyarai sevai. Picturing it thus, I could see the clear harmony between the mudras used as part of “common” tantric ritual, and the mudras and gestures used in dance by the devadasis of old. They were partners in form. Devadasis were the animators of so many moments in a temple’s ritual life; their lallis or other songs accompanied by dance movements and mudras were counterparts to the specialized puja recitations of the priests. That they extended them and elaborated them. Vadivelou sir told me later that the Thiruvarur temple devadasis were known as “Kai kaattum Murai Kari” or “the ones who would show with the hand” (“Thiruvarur Temple Devadasis were traditionally known as “Kai Kaatum Murai Kari.” Aug 19: “According to the Tamil and music scholar B. M. Sundaram, as mentioned in Marabu Vazhi Maanikkangal, they used to perform mudras simultaneously with the temple rituals near the sanctum, without chanting.” This ceiling painting from the Devasiriya Mandapa of the Thyagesa temple in Thiruvarur offers an actual image of such a processional scene, with the Kai Kaattum Murai Karis enacting ritual forms ahead of processional utsavas.)
Until the “system” or “Devadasi culture” if it were ever that cohesive became corrupted and plagued with its own problems, and we destroyed it and killed everything good it ever engendered alongside.

Most people I’ve met in the course of any work in Pondicherry town have a high regard for the devadasis, as powerful women who did a great deal of good in terms of social service. The few remaining, like R. Muthukannammal from Viralimalai, whom Vadivelou sir went to meet and whose videos he shared with me – she was singing songs that had been included by MLV Akka when she prepared the music for Rishi Valley’s Sillapadigaram dance ballet aeons ago, so I knew them – are feted and festooned but nothing about their kalacharam can be recovered by just encouragement at this point. They’re museum relics at best.
Notes here are my reflections on the conversation with Vadivelou Sir, not always sentiments he expressed, though I think he may well share them!

notes.title: Nandikeswara Koyil Pradosham
body: Dr Sanakaradevi’s talks after the bi-weekly pradosham pujas are over at the Nandikeswara temple are always so rich and full of insight. We can rarely sit through them all, but that is no indication of their importance and value to the revitalization of both the Nandikeswara temple practice and to the community as a whole – keep in mind that this temple sits on the edge of what was once the Sankaran kulam, where all the brahmin communities who were associated with the old, un-destroyed Vedapuriswara Koyil once stood. This history is indicated now only by the remnant that is the Shankara Vidyalaya school; all else including the Periya Paarpan and Chinna Paarpan (big and small brahmin) street names are gone, replaced by ostensibly more modern and certainly deracinated ones. Anyway, this evening as we are waiting for prasadam, Dr Sankaradevi recites these lines from Thirumoolar, which reverse the relationship between things–the elephant hides the tree, the elephant is hidden by the tree (in a sculpture). And so on, for Param and this world. Lovely explanation here by G. Sither, who is the very Sither sir I met in Thanjavur once, investigating heritage rice cultivation.
மரத்தை மறைத்தது மாமத யானை மரத்தில் மறைந்தது மாமத யானை பரத்தை மறைத்தன பார்முதல் பூதம் பரத்தில் மறைந்தன பார்முதல் பூதமே

The great furious elephant concealed the wood; Within the wood, the great furious elephant disappeared. The elements, starting with the earth, concealed the Supreme (Param); Within the Supreme, the elements, starting with the earth, disappeared.

notes.title: Nandikeswara Koyil Samadhi Abhishekam
body: This is an amavasya practice at this temple. The samadhi of Sri Jnana Velayudha Swami (Naadu Shanmuga Velayutha Swami) is bathed, sanctified, and readied as with any other abhishekam. A small group of us are at the basement samadhi of the temple. It is humid and stuffy in there, but nothing to be done about that. Murugan’s vel is present. Abhishekam proceeds at its usual pace, with the usual dravyangal or substances. When it is done, we are asked to go upstairs and wait for the alankaram to be completed. It doesn’t take very long. Puja happens then back in the basement. The two priest brothers sing Thiruppugazh, Karuvur / Karur (கருவூர்). As usual, lovely to hear. I take a photo of their phone later, which shows these verses; they sing from this set:
923 — மதியால் வித்தகனாகி (Mathiyaal Vithaganaagi)
924 — இளநீர்க் குவட்டுமுலை (Ilaneerk Kuvattumulai)
925 — தசையாகிய மலவூறல் (Thasaiyagiya Malavooral)
926 — நித்தப் பிணிகொடு மேவிய (Nithap Pinigodu Maeviya)
927 — முட்ட மருட்டி (Mutta Marutti)
928 — சஞ்சல சரித பர நாட்டர்கள் (Sanjala Saritha Para Naattargal)
929 — முகிலள கஞ்சரி யாக்குழை (Mugilalaganjari Yaakkuzhai)

notes.title: Chetty Koyil Amavasya Ul-purappadu
body: The Chetty Koyil also has its amavasya tradition of morning abhishekam taking its Pradosha Nayakar (and Nayaki!) for an ul-purappadu on amavasya nights–one of the 5 days of the Pancha Paruva Utsavam which include these days:
Amavasya (New Moon)
Pournami (Full Moon)
Ravi Sankramana (Masa pirappu or new solar month beginning)
Krishna Paksha Ashtami (or Theipirai Ashtami, 8th day of dark fortnight)
Krishna Paksha Chaturdashi (Sivaratri, 14th day of dark fortnight).

Abhishekam in the morning is to the respective deities, need to be confirmed. We catch the tail end of this observance in the evening, just the ul-purappadu. When Pradosha Nayakar is returned to the main sannathi, there’s a small puja, and then prasadam. No nadaswaram players, only the Brahma talam being kept by Govindarajan. Of course, Sankaranarayana sir is present, as he unfailingly is.

notes.title: Angalamman Koyil Muthialpet Amavasya Unjal Utsavam
body: Angalamman’s amavasya tradition is not in tune with her fierce and forbidding form–she comes out instead and sits on a swing. One can go nearby and move her, as many take joy in doing. There is something gentle and loving about this marking. You don’t fear Her, though she often sits there with astras in her four hands. Thalaattu paattu or lullabies are sung to her. Her fierceness is soothed on this night. I guess after She frees Siva from the brahmahatya dosa (the sin of killing a Brahmin), her anger does not abate that easily–this understanding is so realistic, the anger needs to be specifically quelled and subsided. Because it persists, amavasya is when she is ritually calmed and soothed. One can do this, on this night. It’s not a reception setting as we see at the end of a Brahmotsavam. Unjal utsavams for Devi are of a different character altogether.

Some of these traditions come from Melmalaiyanur, whose Angalamman is the most important in the region (and which site has a specific relation to this temple). Maybe also from Samayapuram, though that is a Mariamman temple (and our Mutthumariamman only marks Pournami, with a small puja for utsavar and ladies coming to read Lalita Sahasranamam).
